caption: The plug of a running heater is yanked out of the wall socket, and a small spark snaps at the prongs as they come out.

sa.check: A heater runs with its plug in a wall socket.
The plug is yanked out of the socket.
A small spark snaps at the prongs as they come out.
The pull is quick: a yank rather than a slow withdrawal.
The spark comes as the plug leaves the socket, not before.

pc.expect: The spark is a single brief flash at the socket at the instant the prongs part from it, and is gone; the heater's glow or fan stops after the plug is out.
pc.fail: The spark glows on at the prongs after the plug is clear of the wall; or sparks appear while the plug is still seated and untouched; or a spark appears at the prongs while the plug lies loose on the floor; or the heater keeps running at full glow to the end of the clip with the plug out.

pc.expect: One plug, one cord, one socket; the plug comes out whole and the socket stays on the wall; the spark leaves nothing behind.
pc.fail: The plug vanishes or a second plug appears; or the socket comes off the wall or vanishes; or the cord splits or detaches; or a glowing dot stays on the wall where the spark was.

pc.expect: Any spark fragments fall from the socket toward the floor and go dark within a short distance.
pc.fail: Sparks rise from the socket and gather above it; or hang in the air; or lie glowing on the floor for the rest of the clip.

pc.expect: The cord follows the plug: it goes slack and drops once the plug is free and stays attached at both ends.
pc.fail: The cord stretches like elastic during the yank; or stands rigid in the air after the plug is out; or the cord floats.

pc.expect: The plug leaves the socket through its holes; the hand and plug pass through nothing; the heater keeps its shape.
pc.fail: The plug passes out through the wall beside the socket; or fingers pass through the plug or the wall; or the heater changes shape; or the plug merges with the socket.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The heater's colour, the socket's design and the wall stay the same.
pc.fail: The heater changes colour; or the socket changes design or moves along the wall; or the cord changes colour.

note: The heater's stopping is read from its visible glow or fan; how quickly it fades is not judged.
